title: Sustainable Finance Policy and Green Capital Markets
summary: An eight-module programme helping policymakers design taxonomies, disclosure regimes, green bond markets and roadmaps that mobilise private capital credibly.
intro: This training programme equips ministries, legislators and public agencies to design credible sustainable finance policy: taxonomies, disclosure, green bond markets, transition plans and the measures that mobilise private capital while managing climate risk to the financial system.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give policymakers a practical understanding of the sustainable finance toolkit, the international standards that underpin it and the trade-offs in applying it nationally. Participants leave able to design a sustainable finance roadmap, decide on taxonomy and disclosure policy, support a credible green bond market, set expectations of regulators on climate risk and guard against greenwashing.
sections.What It Covers: The policy case for sustainable finance, climate risk and the financial system, sustainable finance taxonomies, ISSB disclosure standards and their adoption, green, social and sustainability-linked bonds and sovereign issuance, transition finance and transition plans, greenwashing and investor protection, blended finance and mobilising private capital, and national sustainable finance roadmaps.
Intended Audience: Officials in finance, environment and climate ministries developing sustainable finance and green growth policy
Debt management office staff and public agencies involved in green bond issuance and climate finance
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on sustainability disclosure or climate legislation
Learning Objectives: Explain how climate and nature risks affect the financial system and public finances
Evaluate the design choices for a national or regional sustainable finance taxonomy
Assess options for adopting ISSB standards and wider sustainability disclosure
Describe how labelled bond markets and sovereign green issuance can be developed
Weigh policy tools for mobilising private capital and supporting credible transition
Design a national sustainable finance roadmap with clear roles for government and regulators
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as an intensive programme over two to three days or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with country case studies and policy exercises, ending in a roadmap workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the government's priorities.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services, climate or economic policy is helpful. No technical background in sustainability reporting or climate science is required.
Core Reading: ISSB (2023), IFRS S1 General Requirements for Disclosure of Sustainability-related Financial Information and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures
G20 Sustainable Finance Working Group (2021), G20 Sustainable Finance Roadmap
FSB (2021), FSB Roadmap for Addressing Climate-Related Financial Risks
NGFS (2019), A Call for Action: Climate Change as a Source of Financial Risk
IOSCO (2021), Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Ratings and Data Products Providers: Final Report

modules.title: The Policy Case for Sustainable Finance
modules.summary: Why governments pursue sustainable finance, the scale of the investment gap, and how international commitments and the G20 sustainable finance agenda shape national policy.
objectives: Explain the role of finance in meeting climate and development commitments
Describe the G20 sustainable finance roadmap and the international architecture
Distinguish the roles of government, central banks, regulators and markets
syllabus: Climate and development investment needs and the financing gap
International commitments and nationally determined contributions
G20, FSB, NGFS, ISSB and IOSCO roles in sustainable finance
The sustainable finance policy toolkit at a glance

modules.title: Climate Risk and the Financial System
modules.summary: How physical and transition risks reach banks, insurers, investors and the public balance sheet, and what government should expect of central banks and regulators.
objectives: Explain physical, transition and liability risk transmission channels
Assess the use of climate scenario analysis and stress testing
Identify fiscal risks from climate events and insurance protection gaps
syllabus: Transmission channels to credit, market, insurance and sovereign risk
NGFS scenarios and supervisory climate stress tests
Insurance protection gaps and disaster risk finance
Questions government should ask regulators about climate risk

modules.title: Sustainable Finance Taxonomies
modules.summary: What taxonomies are for, the main design choices from green-only to traffic-light and transition taxonomies, and how to achieve interoperability with major international frameworks.
objectives: Explain the purpose and uses of a sustainable finance taxonomy
Compare design choices on scope, thresholds and transition activities
Assess interoperability and the cost of divergence
syllabus: Taxonomy objectives: classification, disclosure and capital allocation
Technical screening criteria and do-no-significant-harm tests
Transition, amber and social taxonomies
Interoperability and international taxonomy comparisons

modules.title: Sustainability Disclosure and the ISSB Standards
modules.summary: The global baseline for sustainability-related disclosure, the choices government and regulators face in adopting it, and the assurance and capacity issues that follow.
objectives: Explain the requirements of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2
Evaluate adoption options, phasing and proportionality for smaller entities
Assess assurance, data and capacity requirements
syllabus: From TCFD to the ISSB global baseline
Full adoption, partial adoption and phased approaches
Scope 3 emissions, scenario analysis and proportionality
Assurance standards, data infrastructure and market capacity

modules.title: Green Bonds and Sovereign Sustainable Issuance
modules.summary: How green, social, sustainability and sustainability-linked bond markets work, how governments issue sovereign labelled bonds, and the policies that support credible domestic markets.
objectives: Describe the main labelled bond types and market standards
Explain the design and reporting of sovereign green bond frameworks
Evaluate policy support for domestic labelled bond markets
syllabus: Use-of-proceeds and sustainability-linked structures
Sovereign frameworks: eligible expenditure, allocation and impact reporting
External review, verification and labelling standards
Incentives, listings and building the domestic investor base

modules.title: Transition Finance and Transition Plans
modules.summary: How to finance the transition of high-emitting sectors credibly, the role of transition plans for firms and financial institutions, and the policy choices on whether to require them.
objectives: Explain transition finance and the risks of carbon lock-in
Assess the elements of a credible transition plan
Evaluate the case for mandatory or voluntary transition plans
syllabus: Transition pathways for energy, industry and agriculture
Transition plan frameworks for corporates and financial institutions
Just transition and social considerations
Mandatory, comply-or-explain and voluntary approaches

modules.title: Greenwashing, Investor Protection and Market Integrity
modules.summary: How greenwashing arises in products, labels and corporate claims, and the legislative, regulatory and enforcement tools available to protect investors and market credibility.
objectives: Identify common forms of greenwashing in financial products and claims
Evaluate fund labelling, naming and marketing rules
Assess the role of ESG ratings and data providers
syllabus: Greenwashing typologies and enforcement case studies
Sustainable fund labels, naming and marketing standards
ESG ratings and data providers: IOSCO recommendations
Coordinating consumer, securities and competition authorities

modules.title: Mobilising Private Capital and National Roadmaps
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining blended finance, public development banks and other tools to crowd in private capital, and how to build a national sustainable finance roadmap.
objectives: Evaluate blended finance, guarantees and green investment banks
Prioritise policy measures for the national context and sequence them
Produce a national sustainable finance roadmap
syllabus: Blended finance, guarantees and first-loss structures
Public development banks, green investment banks and country platforms
Governance of a roadmap: ministries, regulators and industry
Workshop: a national sustainable finance roadmap
